strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout via cartTotal(items, { coupon }) in src/cart.js: 10% bulk discount at 10+ items (quantities summed), SAVE5 coupon ($5 after bulk, floored at $0, other codes refused), $4.99 shipping unless discounted goods are >= $50, empty cart free. Unit tests with Vitest prove each rule and its boundaries. Reading the code, bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount — a suspected defect against AC1, kept as an expected failure.
inScope: cartTotal, bulkDiscount behaviour in src/cart.js: bulk discount, coupons, shipping, empty cart
outOfScope: Any UI or API for checkout (none exists in the repo)
assumptions: Coupon codes are case-sensitive: only exactly 'SAVE5' is valid (code uses an exact key lookup); 'save5' is refused.
'Refused with an error' means cartTotal throws; tests check the thrown message includes the submitted code (the part the test controls).
Amounts are compared as rounded-to-cents numbers as cartTotal returns them.
Pure unit tests; nothing is faked.
openQuestions: AC1 says 10 or more items get the discount, but src/cart.js uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD` so exactly 10 items get none; TC1 is kept as an expected failure until the code is fixed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (summing line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets none.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, goods never below $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods after discounts are >= $50, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items gets 10% off. bulkDiscount in src/cart.js:22 checks `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items (4 + 6 at $10) is charged $100 instead of $90. The check should be `>=`.
defects.evidence: TC1 (it.fails) asserts cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) toBe(90); the actual value is 100 (expected 100 to be 90).

review.standard: General: recognise the app's behaviour by its structure, not the wording of a message; check the part of the message the test controls, not a prefix every failure shares
review.summary: The refusal assertion matches the app's own wording `coupon: ${code}` instead of just the submitted code, and for the '' row it checks nothing except that shared wording.
review.failureScenario: src/cart.js:30 throws `Unknown coupon: ${coupon}`. If that message is reworded without changing behaviour (for example `Coupon "SAVE10" is not valid`, or `Unknown coupon code SAVE10`), all three it.each rows fail even though every code is still refused and the message still contains the code. The '' row has the opposite problem: the code it controls is empty, so `toContain('coupon: ')` passes for any error whose message contains 'coupon: ', and it doesn't show the submitted code is in the message. Fix: assert `toThrow(code)` for the non-empty codes, without the 'coupon: ' prefix. For '', assert that the call throws an Error, and don't claim the row checks that the message contains the code.

review.standard: Vitest rules: Errors & Callback Assertions — assert throws through the matcher (`expect(() => fn()).toThrow(...)`)
review.summary: The file adds a hand-rolled try/catch `captureError` helper where Vitest's `toThrow` matcher does the same job.
review.failureScenario: The helper is sound because it throws when the call returns, so the tests can't pass wrongly. Still, `expect(() => cartTotal(items, { coupon: code })).toThrow(code)` at line 63 and `.toThrow(Error)` at line 71 would say the same thing with Vitest's own failure messages. Then the extra helper and its custom 'expected the call to throw' error aren't needed.
